question: A primary nurse notices a prescribed drug dose does not match a patient's failing kidneys. What is the best action?

options.A: Wait until the next shift change to let the incoming nurse deal with it.
options.B: Advocate for the patient by contacting the physician to question the safe dosage.
options.C: Administer the medication anyway since the doctor prescribed it.
options.D: Stop all nursing documentation for the day to avoid liability.

explanation: You are the patient's safety net! Always speak up and check with the doctor if a medication dose looks unsafe for your patient's lab results.

question: What is an endemic disease?

options.A: A rare disease that only appears once every century
options.B: A physical injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident
options.C: A medical condition caused entirely by eating too much sugar
options.D: An infection that is constantly present within a specific region

explanation: Endemic diseases, such as malaria in tropical climates, maintain a steady presence in the local area. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is another common term used to describe a brand name drug?

options.A: Generic identifier
options.B: Chemical name
options.C: Universal formula
options.D: Proprietary name

explanation: A brand name is also called a proprietary name because the company 'properly' owns the rights to that specific marketing title.

question: What do we mean when we say an ultrasound is 'operator-dependent'?

options.A: The machine will not turn on unless a licensed physician is in the room
options.B: The accuracy of the results depends heavily on the skill of the person holding the probe
options.C: Patients must pay a separate fee every time the probe touches their skin
options.D: The device requires constant maintenance by an external technician

explanation: Because you have to guide the probe yourself, the picture and diagnosis depend a lot on your scanning technique and practice!

question: How does government-funded agricultural research benefit the general public?

options.A: By ensuring that farming requires zero human labor input
options.B: By developing pest-resistant crops that secure the food supply
options.C: By removing all regulations on chemical pesticide usage
options.D: By discovering new ways to make processed foods last indefinitely

explanation: Research creates stronger, higher-yield crops that protect against harvest failures and maintain stable food availability. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h3)

question: A woman with sickle cell disease is admitted in active labor. What is the most critical nursing action for her care?

options.A: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent swelling
options.B: Encouraging unmedicated natural childbirth at home
options.C: Maintaining strict intravenous hydration
options.D: Keeping the room temperature cold to prevent shivering

explanation: Spot on! Dehydration makes the blood thicker and can easily trigger a crisis, so keeping fluids flowing through an IV is an absolute must.

question: A nurse is assessing a patient who uses a wheelchair full-time. Which oversight represents a common mistake in clinical practice?

options.A: Failing to check routine preventative screenings like blood pressure and dental health
options.B: Asking the patient about their daily routine for bathing and dressing
options.C: Evaluating the patient for chronic muscle spasms and nerve pain
options.D: Inspecting the skin over the sacrum and heels for early redness

explanation: Clinicians often fixate on the visible disability and neglect general preventative healthcare that all patients require. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why is complete chest recoil important between individual chest compressions?

options.A: It keeps the patient's lungs inflated with fresh air
options.B: It gives the rescuer's tired arm muscles a chance to rest
options.C: It prevents the ribs from fracturing during compressions
options.D: It lets the heart chambers fill back up with blood

explanation: If the chest does not recoil fully, the heart cannot refill properly, making the next compression useless. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why are the axillary lymph nodes so important when checking a patient for breast lumps?

options.A: They help fight off skin infections.
options.B: They supply primary blood flow to the nipple.
options.C: They control milk production in the alveoli.
options.D: They are the main path for spreading breast cancer cells.

explanation: Great job thinking critically! Since most breast lymph fluid drains straight to the armpit, nurses always check the axillary lymph nodes first for signs of cancer spread.

question: What do we call it when cancer cells break away and spread to other parts of the body through the blood or lymph system?

options.A: Apoptosis
options.B: Mitosis
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Hyperplasia

explanation: You've got this! Metastasis is simply the word for when cancer travels from its original spot to start new tumors elsewhere. Great job!

question: A patient comes in with diarrhea, stomach cramps, and fatigue. What is an important question to ask during your nursing assessment?

options.A: Inquiring about recent international air travel to Europe
options.B: Checking the patient's family history of genetic blood disorders
options.C: Reviewing past surgical procedures performed in childhood
options.D: Asking about water sources and sanitation practices at home

explanation: Since tummy troubles and parasites are heavily linked to our surroundings, checking how the patient gets their drinking water and manages waste is a great diagnostic clue.

question: Which lab test is most important to check before giving a patient intravenous contrast?

options.A: Coagulation profile
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Fasting blood glucose
options.D: Serum creatinine

explanation: Serum creatinine tells us how well the kidneys are working. Since contrast leaves through the kidneys, we need to make sure they can handle it safely.

question: Why do doctors give antibiotics along with fluids when treating cholera?

options.A: To completely replace the need for drinking water
options.B: To rebuild the muscular lining of the stomach
options.C: To shorten illness duration and reduce bacteria shedding
options.D: To prevent the spread of mosquito vectors

explanation: Antibiotics aren't the main fix (fluids are!), but they help clear the bacteria faster so the patient recovers sooner.

question: How many minutes of moderate exercise per week are generally recommended for primary prevention?

options.A: Exactly 30 minutes
options.B: Up to 500 minutes
options.C: At least 150 minutes
options.D: No more than 60 minutes

explanation: That's right! Health guidelines suggest a minimum of 150 minutes of moderate activity weekly to keep our metabolism humming nicely.

question: What is the main focus of 'pharmacovigilance'?

options.A: Transporting bulk cargo across regional borders
options.B: Monitoring and reporting adverse drug reactions
options.C: Setting international market prices for herbal supplements
options.D: Manufacturing sterile equipment for surgical theatres

explanation: Well done! Pharmacovigilance is just a fancy word for watching out for and reporting drug side effects to keep patients safe.

question: Why would a doctor order an Arterial Blood Gas (ABG) test for an asphyxiated patient?

options.A: To measure blood acidity and gas levels directly
options.B: To screen the blood stream for infectious bacteria
options.C: To count the exact number of red blood cells
options.D: To check if the patient took any prescription drugs

explanation: An ABG gives a direct look at how much oxygen and carbon dioxide are floating around, plus the blood's pH. Super helpful during respiratory distress!

question: Which parts of the body usually show signs of nutritional shortages first?

options.A: Deep dense bones like the femur
options.B: Hard cartilage located in the joints
options.C: Tissues with rapid cell turnover like skin and hair
options.D: Large skeletal muscles in the thighs

explanation: Cells that divide quickly need a constant supply of nutrients, so they show outward signs of shortage first.

question: Which helpful acronym reminds nurses and clients of the warning signs for combined hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: ACHES
options.B: GATHER
options.C: ABCDE
options.D: SBAR

explanation: You got it! ACHES stands for Abdominal pain, Chest pain, Headaches, Eye problems, and Severe leg pain—key warning signs every pill user should watch out for.

question: Which of these instructions is WRONG for a patient going home with a catheter?

options.A: Wash your hands thoroughly before touching the tubing or drainage bag
options.B: Secure the catheter tubing to your thigh to prevent pulling
options.C: Keep the drainage bag higher than the level of your bladder at all times
options.D: Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day unless restricted

explanation: The bag must ALWAYS stay below the bladder! If it's higher, gravity will make the urine flow right back inside the patient. Great catch!

question: A baby is born limp, pale, and quiet after a home delivery. What should you do right away?

options.A: Immediately give the baby back to the mother for skin-to-skin contact
options.B: Wait patiently for five minutes to see if the Apgar score improves
options.C: Call an ambulance without taking any action inside the home
options.D: Provide initial steps of warmth, clearing the airway, and stimulation

explanation: Act fast and stay calm! A baby who isn't breathing needs immediate help: dry them, keep them warm, clear the airway, and gently stimulate them.

question: Why are range-of-motion exercises so important for a stroke patient with limited movement?

options.A: To reverse the original brain damage caused by the stroke
options.B: To speed up the metabolic rate and prevent weight gain
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for any walking aids
options.D: To prevent painful muscle contractures and joint deformities

explanation: Moving those joints keeps them flexible and stops tight muscles from locking up permanently. Great job!

question: Which family planning method category also helps protect against Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal pills
options.B: Barrier methods
options.C: Permanent surgeries
options.D: Intrauterine devices

explanation: Only barrier methods like condoms physically block fluids, which stops both unwanted pregnancy AND pesky STIs. Pills and IUDs do not protect against infections!

question: Why is plotting a child's measurements over time better than taking just a single measurement?

options.A: It is the only legal requirement for pediatric hospital admission
options.B: It reveals individual growth trends rather than just a one-time snapshot
options.C: It eliminates all possible errors made during the weighing process
options.D: It removes the need to use standard growth charts

explanation: Think of it like a movie versus a single photograph. One measurement only shows you right now, but tracking over time shows the real direction and speed of the child's development.

question: Which hormones flood the body during a 'fight or flight' response when a mum is distressed?

options.A: Adrenaline and noradrenaline
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Thyroid stimulating hormones
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: When fear or severe stress hits, the nervous system kicks into gear and releases catecholamines like adrenaline and noradrenaline.

question: Why is understanding how drug classes work so important for patient safety?

options.A: It ensures the hospital pharmacy never runs out of stock
options.B: It allows nurses to manufacture replacement drugs at the nursing station
options.C: It replaces the need to check patient identification bands
options.D: It helps nurses anticipate overlapping side effects and drug interactions

explanation: Knowing drug classes helps you spot dangerous drug combinations or double-up side effects before they cause harm.

question: How does a nurse act as an advocate for the community within the health system?

options.A: By presenting community needs like clean water and drug supplies to authorities
options.B: By punishing villagers who fail to clean their surroundings
options.C: By replacing traditional healers with certified medical doctors
options.D: By keeping all medical supplies locked away in the clinic store

explanation: Advocacy involves speaking up on behalf of the community to ensure higher authorities provide necessary resources and support. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why are regular hearing tests important for workers in noisy industrial plants?

options.A: They detect early hearing loss before the damage becomes permanent
options.B: They make the factory machines run much more quietly
options.C: They prove that loud noise has no effect on human ears
options.D: They replace the need for wearing earplugs

explanation: Routine testing spots subtle hearing changes early, prompting better protection before deafness occurs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: A healthy full-term baby is a few days old. How does blood flow through its heart now compared to inside the womb?

options.A: Deoxygenated blood travels directly back to the placenta via the cord
options.B: Blood bypasses the pulmonary circuit via the open ductus arteriosus
options.C: All blood from the right side now flows entirely through the lungs
options.D: Oxygenated blood continues to cross directly from right to left atrium

explanation: Spot on! With all the baby shunts closed up, the heart circulation is fully independent: the right side pumps blood through the lungs, and the left side pumps it to the body.

question: What is the basic medical definition of urinary incontinence?

options.A: The involuntary loss of urine
options.B: An infection in the urinary tract
options.C: Painful and burning urination
options.D: The complete inability to produce urine

explanation: Urinary incontinence specifically refers to the accidental or involuntary leaking of urine from the bladder. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why should you follow up with your patient after giving an injection?

options.A: To collect the empty plastic syringe for hospital recycling
options.B: To monitor for adverse reactions and local tissue swelling
options.C: To ask the patient to sign a legal satisfaction form
options.D: To measure how fast the muscle tissue heals the puncture

explanation: Wonderful! Checking back helps you catch any early allergic reactions or swelling right away. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: When is the best time to schedule morning care or physical activity for someone with rheumatoid arthritis?

options.A: Early in the morning before any medication is given while stiffness is highest
options.B: Immediately following heavy meals to ensure high energy levels
options.C: Late at night when the client is completely exhausted from the day
options.D: Right after administering morning pain medications and allowing time to take effect

explanation: Giving pain meds a little time to kick in first makes a huge difference! The patient can move around with much less pain and stiffness.

question: What is the first step an effective nurse should take before starting patient counseling?

options.A: Telling the patient everything they are doing wrong in their life
options.B: Handing out a long, detailed textbook on the disease
options.C: Writing a strict prescription without asking any questions
options.D: Assessing what the patient already knows and is willing to change

explanation: Understanding the patient's baseline knowledge and readiness helps the nurse tailor education to be practical and relevant. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h6)

question: What is the main goal of surgical debridement in osteomyelitis?

options.A: To fuse the adjacent joints together permanently
options.B: To stretch the limb to make it longer
options.C: To replace all marrow with synthetic polymers
options.D: To remove dead and infected bone tissue

explanation: Debridement is basically a clean-up operation where the surgeon scrapes away all the dead, infected bone that antibiotics alone can't reach.

question: Which nursing action directly helps get rid of germs on hands and hospital equipment?

options.A: Allowing visitors to share food freely with patients
options.B: Practicing strict hand hygiene and clean techniques
options.C: Discharging all admitted patients right away
options.D: Turning off the AC units in the rooms

explanation: Good hand washing and clean hospital habits sweep away germs before they can set up camp and infect someone.

question: Why is assessment in palliative care an ongoing cycle rather than a one-time thing?

options.A: Hospital policies require daily paperwork updates from the nursing staff
options.B: Patient conditions and symptoms shift as the illness progresses
options.C: Insurance companies demand new symptom scores before paying bills
options.D: Doctors change their minds about medications every few hours

explanation: Because serious illnesses change rapidly, as nurses we need to keep checking in so we can catch new discomforts early.

question: What is the primary purpose of hemostasis in the human body?

options.A: To produce new red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: To pump blood efficiently through the heart
options.C: To transport oxygen and nutrients to body tissues
options.D: To stop bleeding from injured blood vessels

explanation: Hemostasis is the specific physiological response designed to halt bleeding and repair vascular injury. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main difference between emission and ejaculation?

options.A: Emission is controlled by parasympathetic nerves, while erection is sympathetic
options.B: Emission involves only the testes, while ejaculation involves the prostate
options.C: Emission moves fluid into the urethra, while ejaculation expels it outward
options.D: Emission happens before puberty, while ejaculation occurs only in adulthood

explanation: Spot on! Emission gathers and moves the fluid into the upper urethra, while ejaculation uses muscle contractions to push it completely out of the body.

question: When packing a deep wound in a patient's home, what is the golden rule for placing the gauze inside?

options.A: Pack the wound tightly until it is completely firm to stop all bleeding.
options.B: Pack the wound loosely so it fills the space without putting pressure on the tissue.
options.C: Pack the wound using dry cotton balls for maximum absorption.
options.D: Pack only the top layer of skin and leave the deeper cavity empty.

explanation: Remember: never pack too tightly! Packing a wound too firmly cuts off the blood supply those new cells need to heal.

question: Which sensory receptors deep in the skin are great at detecting deep pressure and heavy vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Free nerve endings
options.C: Meissner corpuscles
options.D: Merkel discs

explanation: Spot on! Pacinian corpuscles are shaped like tiny onions and sit deep in the skin to sense firm pressure and vibrations.

question: How do educators officially define true "learning"?

options.A: A permanent change in behavior or knowledge from experience
options.B: Attending all scheduled classroom lectures and clinicals
options.C: Memorizing facts for a nursing board examination
options.D: The physical growth of the brain during young adulthood

explanation: Learning isn't just about growing older or cramming for a test—it's when your actual knowledge or actions shift because of real experiences. You've got this!

question: What strategy is often successful when working with religious leaders to stop harmful traditional customs?

options.A: Replacing traditional ceremonies with foreign cultural festivals
options.B: Reviewing texts to show the practices are cultural, not religious
options.C: Threatening them with immediate excommunication from society
options.D: Banning all places of worship that question government policies

explanation: Many harmful practices are falsely claimed as religious mandates; examining texts helps separate faith from harmful custom. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h4)

question: Which health worker helps patients learn how to dress, cook, and do daily chores again?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Oncology social worker
options.C: Speech-language pathologist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Great job! Occupational therapists (OTs) focus on everyday life skills and help patients master their daily self-care tasks independently.

question: Which viral enzyme helps convert the virus's RNA into DNA?

options.A: Protease
options.B: Integrase
options.C: DNA polymerase
options.D: Reverse transcriptase

explanation: Well done! Because HIV works 'in reverse' from RNA to DNA, it relies on an enzyme called reverse transcriptase to do the trick. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h3)

question: What does agglutination mean when performing a forward blood typing test?

options.A: The plasma separates completely from the solid blood components
options.B: The blood sample destroys itself due to lack of adequate nutrition
options.C: The red blood cells change their normal shape into sickle cells
options.D: The red blood cells clump together in the presence of matching antibodies

explanation: Agglutination is the visible clumping that occurs when antibodies bind to their specific matching antigens on red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the main difference between HIV and AIDS?

options.A: HIV only affects children, while AIDS affects adults.
options.B: AIDS is curable, whereas HIV infection remains lifelong.
options.C: AIDS is the advanced stage of HIV infection marked by severe immune damage.
options.D: HIV is sexually transmitted, while AIDS is contracted through blood only.

explanation: Think of HIV as the virus, and AIDS as the advanced stage when the immune system gets very weak. Keep pushing!

question: Why do many women in Nigeria still resort to unsafe abortions despite strict laws?

options.A: Abortion being completely free in government hospitals
options.B: Desire to experience traditional surgical practices
options.C: Lack of access to safe services and modern contraceptives
options.D: Legal encouragement from local community leaders

explanation: Spot on! When family planning services and safe care are hard to reach, vulnerable women sadly turn to dangerous alternatives.

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) mainly work in the body?

options.A: By putting the central nervous system to sleep
options.B: By releasing natural endorphins in the spine
options.C: By attaching straight to brain opioid receptors
options.D: By blocking prostaglandins at the injury site

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen stop the body from making prostaglandins—the chemical helpers that cause swelling and pain right where you got hurt.

question: Which nursing care measure is especially important to prevent blood clots right after delivery for a patient with sickle cell disease?

options.A: Stopping all pain medications immediately after delivery
options.B: Restricting fluid intake to decrease postpartum swelling
options.C: Encouraging early mobilization and preventing blood clots
options.D: Applying ice packs to the abdomen to slow down blood flow

explanation: Wonderful! Getting the mum moving early after delivery is a fantastic way to keep her circulation healthy and ward off nasty blood clots.

question: Which physical sign strongly points toward a uterine perforation or pelvic peritonitis?

options.A: Painless bilateral swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Generalized skin rash and localized itching
options.C: Elevated blood pressure and clear breath sounds
options.D: A rigid and tender abdomen with rebound tenderness

explanation: When the lining of the belly (peritoneum) gets irritated or infected, the abdominal muscles lock up tight ('rigidity'), and pressing and letting go hurts sharply ('rebound tenderness'). A classic exam and ward clue!

question: What is the biggest benefit of a psychologically safe work culture on the ward?

options.A: Employees never experience any form of physical fatigue or tiredness.
options.B: Patients are discharged from the hospital twice as fast.
options.C: Hospital operating costs are reduced to absolute zero immediately.
options.D: Staff feel comfortable reporting near-misses without fear of harsh punishment.

explanation: When people aren't terrified of being yelled at, they will speak up about close calls or mistakes. That open communication is what keeps patients truly safe!

question: Which lab test is most commonly used to confirm a Lassa virus infection?

options.A: Microscopic stool examination for ova
options.B: Sputum acid-fast bacilli smear
options.C: Electrocardiogram rhythm strip
options.D: Reverse Transcription-Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR)

explanation: RT-PCR checks for viral RNA in the blood with great accuracy, making it the gold standard for confirmation.

question: Why do young women and girls often face a higher risk of new HIV infections in many communities?

options.A: Males do not contract the virus due to protective antibodies.
options.B: Biological differences and social inequalities intersect to increase their risk.
options.C: Healthcare workers screen boys less frequently than girls.
options.D: Females possess a genetic immunity that wears off during puberty.

explanation: Well done! Young women face both physical vulnerabilities and social factors like gender inequality that make it harder to negotiate safe sex.

question: What is the most common and immediate cause of death after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Hemorrhage
options.B: Uterine cancer
options.C: Renal failure
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Heavy, uncontrolled bleeding is the number one emergency here. When tissues are torn or left behind in unsterile procedures, severe bleeding can turn fatal very quickly if we don't act fast.

question: Why do nurses need to check and re-check a patient's physical abilities regularly during cancer care?

options.A: Therapists need to change their billing codes frequently
options.B: Initial assessments are usually inaccurate due to stress
options.C: Hospital accreditation requires weekly paperwork updates
options.D: A patient's functional status can fluctuate rapidly during treatment

explanation: Because treatments and cancer can change a patient's strength quickly up or down, regular check-ins help us keep our care plan on track.

question: What does peripheral resistance refer to in the circulatory system?

options.A: Fluid loss through capillary pores
options.B: Friction of blood against vessel walls
options.C: The pumping strength of the left atrium
options.D: The speed of oxygen binding to hemoglobin

explanation: Peripheral resistance is the drag or friction blood experiences as it travels through the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why should a nurse adjust the weighing scale to zero before weighing every child?

options.A: To make the scale display readings in kilograms instead of pounds
options.B: To comply with international manufacturer warranties
options.C: To calm the child down before the measurement process begins
options.D: To prevent small errors from accumulating between readings

explanation: Always zeroing your scale clears any leftover weight from the previous patient, keeping your numbers accurate every time.

question: What causes that unpleasant smell in some gas?

options.A: Sulfur compounds produced by specific gut bacteria
options.B: The breakdown of proteins by liver enzymes
options.C: High levels of pure oxygen from swallowed air
options.D: Undigested stomach acid reaching the rectum

explanation: Certain helpful (and smelly!) bacteria release tiny amounts of sulfur when they break down food. Totally normal body process!

question: When a patient experiences a permanent sensory loss, what emotional and psychological response do nurses frequently need to help them manage?

options.A: Grief, social withdrawal, and depression
options.B: Severe memory loss and confusion about time
options.C: Aggression and physical violence toward staff
options.D: Euphoria and unrealistic optimism about recovery

explanation: Losing sight or hearing is a massive life change. Patients often go through a grieving process and might pull away from others, so our empathetic nursing support is crucial here.

question: In a busy emergency unit, why do nurses grab the glucometer so quickly?

options.A: It stops the liver from making extra glucose
options.B: It proves whether the patient has diabetes permanently
options.C: It replaces the need for a full medical history
options.D: It helps spot dangerous high or low sugar levels fast

explanation: Portable glucometers give you results in seconds. Catching a dangerously high or low blood sugar early lets you step in and save the day!

question: What is the very first practical safety step before applying a prepared warm poultice to a patient?

options.A: Wrap the entire body in thick blankets
options.B: Test the temperature of the mixture
options.C: Leave the room for thirty minutes
options.D: Scrub the skin hard with stiff wire wool

explanation: Always test the temperature to prevent accidental burns before the substance touches the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h6)

question: Roughly how long is the plasma half-life of levothyroxine in a healthy person?

options.A: About six hours
options.B: About seven days
options.C: Twenty-four hours
options.D: Fourteen days

explanation: Because it hangs around in the body for about a week, patients only need to take it once a day. But it also means it takes a few weeks to adjust when a dose is changed!

question: Why do experts now believe the cerebellum is also involved in mental tasks, not just physical movement?

options.A: It stores all semantic memory traces gathered during childhood
options.B: It produces the majority of dopamine used in the frontal lobes
options.C: It generates conscious thoughts independently of the cerebral cortex
options.D: It maintains extensive neural loops connecting with prefrontal and limbic brain regions

explanation: The cerebellum doesn't just talk to motor areas; it connects with thinking and emotional centers too, helping influence our mood, memory, and language! Fascinating, right?

question: Why is an IUD called a long-acting reversible contraceptive?

options.A: It only prevents pregnancy for a maximum of three months
options.B: It is permanent and cannot be taken out once inserted
options.C: It requires taking daily pills to stay effective
options.D: It protects against pregnancy for years, but fertility returns after removal

explanation: You get years of steady protection, but if the client ever wants to get pregnant later, you just take it out and her natural fertility bounces right back!

question: What happens when a drug is tightly attached to blood proteins?

options.A: It cannot cross capillary walls to reach its target tissue
options.B: It is instantly destroyed by white blood cells
options.C: It causes a rapid, dangerous spike in blood pressure
options.D: It filters out through the kidneys in minutes

explanation: Protein-bound drugs are like big passengers that can't fit through the tiny gaps in blood vessels. They stay inactive in the blood until they let go of the protein.

question: How does severe malnutrition negatively impact a community's immune status?

options.A: It directly destroys the skin's physical ability to sweat
options.B: It prevents infants from absorbing breast milk antibodies
options.C: It speeds up the rate at which vaccines expire in storage
options.D: It impairs the body's ability to produce antibodies and immune cells

explanation: Nutrients are the building blocks of the immune system; lacking them stops the body from making enough cells and antibodies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the immediate impact of early marriage on a young girl's education?

options.A: Immediate promotion to higher academic grades
options.B: An abrupt end to her formal education
options.C: Free government-funded university placement
options.D: Mandatory transfer to an adult night school

explanation: Spot on! Heavy household chores and early pregnancies almost always force young brides to drop out of school for good.

question: How do azole antifungal drugs stop fungi from growing?

options.A: By stopping the production of essential fungal proteins
options.B: By destroying the genetic material inside the fungal nucleus
options.C: By creating physical holes in the fungal cell wall
options.D: By blocking an enzyme needed to make ergosterol

explanation: Azoles block the factory worker (enzyme) that builds ergosterol. Without ergosterol, the fungus can't maintain its cell wall and dies.

question: Which communication tool helps stop a nurse from making wrong assumptions about a patient's home life?

options.A: Relying strictly on family member reports
options.B: Asking open-ended questions
options.C: Avoiding conversation during physical exams
options.D: Using closed-ended yes or no questions

explanation: Spot on! Open questions let patients tell their own stories in their own words without us putting words in their mouths.

question: What is the main focus of community-centred nursing care?

options.A: Promoting health within people's living environments
options.B: Conducting laboratory tests for rare diseases
options.C: Managing hospital emergency room admissions
options.D: Treating severe illnesses inside hospital wards

explanation: Community-centred care focuses on meeting people in their homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces to promote health rather than waiting for them to arrive at a hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why are antibiotics often started right away before lab results are even back?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of laboratory diagnostic supplies
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for any follow-up testing
options.C: To cure viral infections like herpes simplex immediately
options.D: To stop the infection from spreading upward into the reproductive tract

explanation: Starting treatment fast prevents the infection from traveling up into the uterus and fallopian tubes, avoiding bigger problems later.

question: Why do many lung diseases cause sharp chest pain only when the patient takes a deep breath?

options.A: Air is getting trapped inside the stomach muscles
options.B: The main airway is swelling shut during inhalation
options.C: The heart muscle is stretching too hard against the ribcage
options.D: The inflamed lining of the lungs rubs against the chest wall during movement

explanation: Think of it like a skin scrape rubbing against clothing: when the pleural lining of the lungs gets inflamed, every deep breath causes those sore layers to rub together and hurt!

question: What is the name of the simple hollow tube that gives rise to the central nervous system in the early embryo?

options.A: Neural tube
options.B: Mesodermal cord
options.C: Ectodermal plate
options.D: Notochord

explanation: The human brain and spinal cord originate from the neural tube during early embryonic development. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which instruction should a nurse give a patient regarding pelvic rest after an MVA?

options.A: Avoid eating solid food for at least 48 hours post-procedure
options.B: Keep taking vaginal douches daily to clean out old blood
options.C: Exercise strenuously starting the very next morning
options.D: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for about two weeks

explanation: To prevent bacteria from entering the healing cervix and causing an infection, patients are advised against putting anything in the vagina for two weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical focus of occupational health nursing?

options.A: Managing pediatric developmental milestones in schools
options.B: Promoting the use of proper personal protective equipment
options.C: Inspecting work areas for ergonomic strain and safety risks
options.D: Identifying workplace hazards like toxic chemicals

explanation: Occupational health deals specifically with worker safety and workplace hazards, not school-aged child development. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of feeding hungry children at school?

options.A: Elimination of all infectious skin diseases
options.B: Increased physical height within one week
options.C: Guaranteed automatic promotion to the next grade
options.D: Improved concentration and classroom participation

explanation: You nailed it! A well-fed child has the brain energy needed to focus, answer questions, and join in class activities.

question: What are the three golden rules of radiation safety?

options.A: Light, heat, and pressure
options.B: Height, weight, and volume
options.C: Time, distance, and shielding
options.D: Speed, velocity, and mass

explanation: Always remember: spend less time near radiation, step back to create distance, and use lead shielding. Safety first!

question: What is the main difference between a CT scan and a regular X-ray?

options.A: It requires no computer processing at all
options.B: It uses sound waves instead of radiation
options.C: It only images the superficial skin layers
options.D: It creates cross-sectional slice images

explanation: While both use X-rays, a regular X-ray gives a flat, 2D shadow, but a CT scan gives detailed cross-sectional slices like slicing a loaf of bread. Great job!

question: When is a patient usually transitioned off a soft diet?

options.A: As soon as they request spicy foods
options.B: When their mouth heals and they can chew normally
options.C: On the very first day of hospital admission
options.D: When they refuse to drink water

explanation: The soft diet is temporary and ends once the underlying issue, such as mouth surgery or sore gums, has resolved. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h8)

question: Testicular cancer is most commonly diagnosed in which age group?

options.A: Young men aged 15 to 35
options.B: Middle-aged men aged 50 to 65
options.C: Pre-pubertal boys under 10
options.D: Elderly men over 75 years

explanation: Good to know! Unlike many other cancers, testicular cancer hits younger guys, which is why teaching self-exams to this group is so vital.

question: What are the tiny, baby worms produced by adult Onchocerca volvulus called?

options.A: Sporozoites
options.B: Trophozoites
options.C: Cercariae
options.D: Microfilariae

explanation: Spot on! The adult female worms release millions of microfilariae, which then travel through the skin and eye tissues, causing those troublesome symptoms.

question: A patient in the emergency ward has a racing heart, high blood pressure, and extreme restlessness after taking a drug. What kind of drug is most likely behind this?

options.A: Barbiturates
options.B: Depressants
options.C: Cannabinoids
options.D: Stimulants

explanation: Spot on! Stimulants like cocaine or amphetamines rev up the nervous system, leading to high energy, fast heart rates, and agitation.

question: What should you do if the chosen injection site has an open sore or infection?

options.A: Warm the skin with a hot pack to improve blood flow
options.B: Choose a different healthy site for the injection
options.C: Use a longer needle to bypass the damaged area
options.D: Clean the sore with extra antiseptic before piercing

explanation: Always protect broken skin! Finding a healthy site prevents spreading infection and helps the medication absorb properly.

question: A student nurse is assigned to give medications on the ward. What is the correct way to supervise this task?

options.A: Provide direct clinical supervision while medications are given
options.B: Allow senior patients to help the student verify doses
options.C: Delegate the supervision entirely to the ward cleaner
options.D: Let the student complete all drug rounds independently

explanation: Students must always be supervised by qualified staff to protect patient safety during clinical procedures. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is a common long-term problem after severe injury and healing of the voice box (larynx)?

options.A: Loss of the sense of smell and taste
options.B: Spontaneous closure of the food pipe
options.C: Airway narrowing (stenosis) from scar tissue
options.D: Permanent widening of the windpipe

explanation: You got it! As damaged tissues heal, extra scar formation can contract and narrow the airway passage, causing breathing trouble later.

question: Which vitamin is especially important in early pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects in the baby?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Folate
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: You nailed it! Folate (or folic acid) is vital during the early weeks of pregnancy to help the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly.

question: Why is strict waste segregation vital during home visits?

options.A: It prevents the spread of infection to the family and community
options.B: It eliminates the need for hand washing after care
options.C: It makes the nurse finish the visit much faster
options.D: It reduces the total weight of the home visiting kit bag

explanation: Separating infectious and hazardous waste stops germs from spreading into the local environment and harming others. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h5)

question: A ward records 50 patients with hypertension out of 200 patients screened. What percentage is that?

options.A: 20 percent
options.B: 10 percent
options.C: 25 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Brilliant! 50 divided by 200 gives you 0.25, which translates nicely to 25 percent.

question: How do nondepolarizing neuromuscular blockers stop a muscle from contracting?

options.A: By sitting on the receptors and preventing acetylcholine from attaching
options.B: By binding to receptors and holding the muscle in a constant state of spasm
options.C: By destroying acetylcholine before it reaches the nerve ending
options.D: By draining all the calcium stores directly out of the muscle fibers

explanation: Think of nondepolarizing blockers as gatecrashers sitting in the chair so acetylcholine can't get a seat. No binding means no muscle movement!

question: A postpartum mum complains of calf pain and swelling in one leg. What serious condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Normal postpartum cramping
options.B: Severe breast engorgement
options.C: Uterine subinvolution
options.D: Deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Spot on! Pain, warmth, and swelling in just one leg are classic red flags for a deep vein thrombosis (DVT). It needs quick medical attention to keep our patient safe!

question: Why is transparency in reporting health funds crucial for community partnerships?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any volunteer labor in the school
options.B: It ensures that teachers receive higher bonuses each month
options.C: It prevents the government from inspecting school facilities
options.D: It builds mutual trust and encourages continued community support

explanation: When communities see how resources are used honestly, they remain willing to support and fund future school health projects. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h7)

question: How can a nurse best support a burnt-out family caregiver who is stressed about feeding duties?

options.A: Blaming the caregiver for the patient's poor nutritional status
options.B: Telling the caregiver to stop worrying and let the patient starve
options.C: Taking over all household chores permanently without involving family
options.D: Connecting caregivers with respite care and community support resources

explanation: Caregivers need a break too! Linking them with support and respite care helps them rest so they can continue providing great care safely.

question: What is the correct sequence of the three stages in the General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS)?

options.A: Alarm reaction, exhaustion, resistance
options.B: Alarm reaction, resistance, exhaustion
options.C: Resistance, exhaustion, alarm reaction
options.D: Exhaustion, alarm reaction, resistance

explanation: Easy to remember: First you sound the Alarm, then you Try to resist it, and if it won't stop, your body reaches Exhaustion.

question: What is a major social factor that makes an older adult more vulnerable to abuse?

options.A: Active community involvement
options.B: Regular attendance at family gatherings
options.C: Social isolation
options.D: Living in an urban apartment

explanation: When an older adult is cut off from friends and community, there are fewer eyes around to spot and report mistreatment. Makes total sense, right?

question: How does heparin mainly work in the body?

options.A: By activating antithrombin III
options.B: By binding directly to blood platelets
options.C: By blocking calcium ion absorption
options.D: By depleting dietary vitamin K

explanation: Heparin teams up with a helper in your blood called antithrombin III to quickly put the brakes on clotting factors. Keep up the great studying!

question: What is the main reason for filling out an ADR form in the hospital?

options.A: To provide data that helps regulatory bodies protect public safety
options.B: To penalize the pharmaceutical company that manufactured the drug
options.C: To prove that the nurse administered the correct medication dosage
options.D: To secure financial compensation for the affected patient

explanation: Every time you report an adverse reaction, you help build a national database that authorities use to track safety trends and protect the public.

question: Why is the spinal epidural space considered a real space, while the cranial epidural space inside the head is just a potential space?

options.A: The spinal cord does not have any meningeal layers surrounding it like the brain does.
options.B: The cranial dura is tightly fused to the skull bones, whereas the spinal dura is not fused to the vertebrae.
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid fills the cranial epidural space constantly during daily life.
options.D: The spinal dura mater lacks any blood vessels or fatty padding beneath the bone.

explanation: You're learning fast! In your skull, the dura is glued tightly to the bone. But in your spine, there is an actual cushion of fat and veins around the dura, making it a true space.

question: Where are the parathyroid glands located?

options.A: Inside the left and right ventricles of the heart
options.B: On the posterior surface of the thyroid gland
options.C: At the upper poles of both adrenal glands
options.D: Suspended within the lower lobes of the lungs

explanation: You'll find these four tiny glands resting right on the back (posterior) side of your thyroid gland in the neck. You've got this!

question: What does 'capacity building' by an NGO usually look like in a community?

options.A: Auditing government financial accounts annually
options.B: Replacing all doctors with foreign medical specialists
options.C: Constructing large teaching hospitals in major capital cities
options.D: Training local volunteers and birth attendants to educate communities

explanation: Capacity building is all about empowering locals! By teaching community members new skills, health programs can keep running long after the NGO leaves.

question: What is the primary purpose of the review of systems in health history taking?

options.A: To perform the physical hands-on examination of the body
options.B: To discharge the patient from the hospital ward
options.C: To uncover symptoms the patient may have forgotten or overlooked
options.D: To administer prescribed medications to the patient

explanation: The review of systems uses a systematic checklist to catch extra details the patient did not bring up initially. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: How should the normal esophagus appear on a healthy barium swallow image?

options.A: A wide pouch with multiple jagged blockages
options.B: A rigid, non-moving tube with thickened walls
options.C: A smooth, straight tubular structure with uniform width
options.D: A completely closed channel with zero contrast entry

explanation: A healthy esophagus shows an even, smooth column of barium moving down without unusual narrowing, widening, or pouching. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the permanent adult name for the leftover, closed-up ductus venosus inside the liver?

options.A: Medial umbilical ligament
options.B: Ligamentum venosum
options.C: Fossa ovalis
options.D: Ligamentum teres

explanation: You've got it! Once that old fetal bypass inside the liver shuts down for good, it turns into a fibrous little band known as the ligamentum venosum.

question: What is the correct speed (rate) for giving breaths during neonatal positive pressure ventilation (PPV)?

options.A: 20 to 30 breaths per minute
options.B: 40 to 60 breaths per minute
options.C: 10 to 15 breaths per minute
options.D: 80 to 100 breaths per minute

explanation: When assisting a baby's breathing, aim for a steady, rhythmic pace of 40 to 60 breaths per minute to match a healthy newborn.

question: What type of language should a nurse use when documenting physical exam findings?

options.A: Vague and generalized terms like 'fine'
options.B: Subjective opinions about the patient's attitude
options.C: Clear, objective, and descriptive language
options.D: Complex poetic metaphors to describe wounds

explanation: Objective descriptions prevent confusion and provide clear facts for other healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: Which layer of the heart wall does the actual hard work of pumping blood?

options.A: Pericardium
options.B: Endocardium
options.C: Myocardium
options.D: Epicardium

explanation: The myocardium is made of strong muscle tissue. Every time your heart beats, it's the myocardium doing the heavy lifting to push blood out!

question: A patient comes in feeling constantly exhausted, has gained weight, hates cold weather, and has dry, coarse hair. What condition do these signs point to?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Hyperthyroidism
options.C: Cushing's syndrome
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: You've got this! These are classic signs of a sluggish metabolism caused by not having enough thyroid hormones in the body.

question: What major part of a person's life is often shaken when a physical disability happens suddenly?

options.A: Their worldview and sense of identity
options.B: Their baseline laboratory blood values
options.C: Their physical height and bone density
options.D: Their cellular immune system response

explanation: A sudden disability turns a person's world upside down, changing how they see themselves and their future. Empathy goes a long way here!

question: A patient with diabetes mellitus develops peripheral neuropathy. Which symptom would you most expect to see?

options.A: Instant spastic paralysis of both upper extremities
options.B: Rapid increase in cognitive processing speed
options.C: Loss of voluntary control over heart contractions
options.D: Numbness and loss of protective sensation in the feet

explanation: Peripheral neuropathy frequently robs patients of sensation in their hands and feet, which is why daily foot checks are so crucial in nursing care for diabetics!

question: Why are standard Alzheimer's drugs usually avoided or used carefully in Pick's disease?

options.A: They accelerate memory loss within the first week of use.
options.B: They interfere with routine blood pressure medications.
options.C: They do not target the underlying pathology and can worsen agitation.
options.D: They cause immediate and permanent paralysis of the lower limbs.

explanation: Alzheimer's medications don't help frontotemporal issues and can actually make behavioral outbursts worse. It's a great clinical pearl to remember for your exams!

question: A nurse notices the clinic frequently runs out of safety boxes, causing staff to leave used needles on trays. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Ignore the issue since it does not affect direct patient treatment
options.B: Report the supply shortage to management and request immediate replenishment
options.C: Tell staff to begin washing and reusing the disposable needles instead
options.D: Instruct patients to bring their own plastic containers from home

explanation: Being a nurse advocate means speaking up when safety supplies run low so we can protect our healthcare team and our community. Great clinical leadership!

question: Which agency is primarily responsible for regulating drugs in Nigeria?

options.A: NMA
options.B: FMOH
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: NMNC

explanation: NAFDAC is our frontline agency charged with checking and controlling food, drugs, cosmetics, and medical devices across Nigeria.

question: Why are deep breathing exercises so important for a patient stuck on bed rest in traction?

options.A: They relax tight muscles to stop spasms
options.B: They stimulate blood flow inside the deep calf veins
options.C: They expand the lungs fully to prevent mucus buildup and collapse
options.D: They increase the pulling force of the traction weights

explanation: Thinking like a real nurse! Lying in bed slows down breathing, which can cause lung issues. Deep breaths keep the tiny air sacs open and clear out mucus.

question: As a nurse assisting with an ultrasound-guided needle procedure, what is your most important duty?

options.A: Adjusting the machine's sound frequency during the scan
options.B: Keeping the area strictly sterile and helping the patient stay still
options.C: Giving the patient general anesthesia
options.D: Reading and writing the final report

explanation: Invasive bedside procedures need strict infection control and a steady patient to keep everything safe and accurate.
